answer: The plume multiplier is published, charged in falcon, and raven lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 1971 identities would post 3089 proofs and burn roughly 27 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
